5                            SAN JOSE DIVISION

7    VALEO SCHALTER UND SENSOREN      Case No.  23-cv-05721-PCP (VKD)     
     GMBH,                                                                
8                                     ORDER GRANTING MOTION FOR           
               Plaintiff,             LEAVE TO FILE VALEO’S REPONSES      
9                                     TO NVIDIA’S INTERROGATORY           
           v.                         NOS. 6 AND 7; SEALING PORTIONS      
10                                     OF THE RESPONSES                    
     NVIDIA CORPORATION,                                                  
                                      Re: Dkt. Nos. 74, 75, 76, 79        
11                                                                         
               Defendant.                                                 

12                                                                         
13        On August 8, 2024, defendant NVIDIA Corporation (“NVIDIA”) filed an administrative 
14   motion seeking leave to file plaintiff Valeo Schalter und Sensoren GmbH’s (“Valeo”) responses to 
15   NVIDIA’s Interrogatory Nos. 6 and 7 in support of a pending discovery dispute.  Dkt. No. 74.  On 
16   August 12, 2024, Valeo filed a response stating that it “does not believe the material is relevant” 
17   but “does not object or oppose if the Court wishes to review this material as it is referenced in the 
18   letter brief.”  Dkt. No. 77 at 1.  NVIDIA’s motion for leave is granted.  
19        Concurrent with the motion for leave, NVIDIA filed two motions asking the Court to seal 
20   portions of the interrogatory responses.  Dkt. Nos. 75, 76.  On August 15, 2024, Valeo filed a 
21   statement in support of NVIDIA’s motions to seal, indicating the portions of the responses for 
22   which it requests sealing.  Dkt. No. 79.                              
23        There is a strong presumption in favor of access by the public to judicial records and 
24   documents accompanying dispositive motions that can be overcome only by a showing of 
25   “compelling reasons supported by specific factual findings.”  Kamakana v. City & Cnty. Of 
26   Honolulu, 447 F.3d 1172, 1178-79 (9th Cir. 2006) (cleaned up).  However, the presumption does 
27   not apply equally to a motion addressing matters that are only “tangentially related to the merits of 
    1    party seeking to seal documents or information in connection with such a motion must meet the 
    2  ||  lower “good cause” standard of Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(c).  Id. at 1098-99; Kamakana, 447 F.3d at 
    3    1179-80.  The discovery matters at issue here do not address the merits of either party’s claims or 
    4  ||  defenses, so the Court applies the “good cause” standard of Rule 26(c). 
    5          NVIDIA asserts that the information it seeks to seal concerns “the confidential names of 
    6 ||  files and functions found in NVIDIA’s proprietary source code” and that public disclosure of this 
    7    information could result in “a competitive disadvantage.”  Dkt. No. 75 at 2.  Valeo states that the 
    8  || portions it seeks to seal involve “pictures of Valeo’s highly confidential, proprietary, and 
    9  || competitive technical information” as well as “the structures and names of folders of information 
   10  || comprising Valeo’s trade secret source code.”  Dkt. No. 79 at 2-3.  Valeo asserts that public 
   11    disclosure of this information “would cause competitive harm.”  Jd. at 3. 
a    12          The Court agrees that good cause exists to seal the designated portions of the interrogatory 

     13    responses.  The redactions proposed to the public version of the document are minimal and 

 v   14    narrowly tailored to address the concerns identified.  See Civil L.R. 79-5(c)(3).  The Court orders 

    15    that the following material be sealed: 
   16
    17 
                                     oo.         .                            . 
         Valeo’s Second Supplemental Objections | Portions of the document highlighted in yellow 
Z    18     and Responses to NVIDIA’s First Set of  | (Dkt. No. 75-3 SEALED) 
   19     Interrogatories (Nos. 6, 7)               Portions of the pictures redacted on page numbers 
                                             10, 11, and 12 (Dkt. No. 79-2) 
   20 
   21          A redacted version of the document is already available on the public docket.  See Dkt. No. 
   22  || 79-2.  Accordingly, no further action is required. 
   23          IT IS SO ORDERED. 
   9A    Dated: August 16, 2024 
   25
   26 
                                                        Virginia K. DeMarchi 
   27                                                    United States Magistrate Judge
